subject: SLA baseline exception + latency-floor ask for batched endpoints
messages:
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@skyward.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: SLA baseline exception + latency floors for batch endpoints

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Skyward is excited about Redwood’s latency and cost story for large-batch scoring. Before we move to legal, procurement has one asks on the standard SLA template: our workload has a high proportion of scheduled batch inference (nightly and hourly jobs) and we need two clarifications/exceptions:

1) Latency floor carveout — request that 99th percentile latency commitments be measured only against interactive (non-batched) endpoints. For batched endpoints we propose a separate latency floor of 300ms p99 per-token equivalent, because batching intentionally trades latency for throughput.

2) Monthly credit cap — we can accept service credits, but procurement wants a hard cap at 10% of monthly invoice for the first 12 months while we ramp.

I attached a short summary (Skyward_SLA_change_request.pdf) and a proposed contract markup. Can you route this to the SLA/pricing team and let us know if these are deal-breakers? We’re aiming to sign by end of month.

Also please confirm SOC 2 in-scope evidence (report or letter) and the contact for security questionnaires.

Thanks,
Amelia Ross
Head of Procurement — Skyward Analytics
amelia.ross@skyward.io
procurement@skyward.io

--

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@skyward.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA baseline exception + latency floors for batch endpoints

Amelia —

Really appreciate the clear write-up and the quick timeline. Looping in Ben (sales) and Laura (contracts) so we can respond holistically. A few quick notes while we pull the redline together:

- SOC 2 Type II is available; I’ll have our security team send the report or an attestation letter to you directly by EOD tomorrow.
- The latency-floor carveout for batched endpoints is reasonable in principle — we want to preserve guarantees for interactive apps, while acknowledging batch patterns.
- On the credit cap, we typically offer a cap but can discuss phasing (e.g., 8% cap for first 6 months then 12-month review) depending on commitment level.

Ben/Laura — can you take the attached and propose a concrete language change and credit cap that keeps the commercial risk in check? Amelia, we’ll aim to share a redlined SLA and a proposal by Monday.

Best,
Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@skyward.io>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA baseline exception + latency floors for batch endpoints

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear proposal and timeline. I reviewed Skyward_SLA_change_request.pdf and spoke with Markus and ops. Here’s a counterproposal we think balances predictability and operational reality: 

1) Latency measurement scope: keep the standard 99th-percentile latency commitment for "interactive endpoints" (defined as any route with median observed latency < 100ms during sample window). For "batch endpoints" (explicitly labelled in the API config), we will:
  - Exclude batch-labeled routes from interactive latency SLO calculations.
  - Add an alternate benchmark clause: batch p99 latency target of 300ms per-token-equivalent under steady-state load, measured on a 24-hour sample window. Batch endpoints are exempt from uptime-triggered credits when the monthly traffic share of batch requests exceeds 30% of total tokens.

2) Monthly service credit cap: we can accept a capped remedy of 8% of monthly invoice for the first 6 months, then reassess at month 6 for extension/adjustment. If Skyward commits to a minimum monthly spend tier (TBD in SOW) we can raise the cap to 10%.

3) Operational commitments: We will provide a runbook for scheduled large-batch jobs and a dedicated onboarding checkpoint with our SRE team to tune autoscaling to reduce correlated impact.

I’ve asked Laura to produce a redline with the language above and a short fallback paragraph for extraordinary maintenance windows. We’re attaching Redwood_SLA_Redline_v2.docx.

If this looks ok, we can push to DocuSign and include the PO. Appreciate the quick cadence — we should be able to get this executed within your month-end goal if procurement and legal are aligned.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales, Redwood Inference

--On Mon, Nov 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@skyward.io> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs: if batch endpoints are exempt from uptime-triggered credits when batch share >30%, how will we measure mixed traffic routes that sometimes serve both interactive and scheduled traffic?
> 
> Also can we get the PO template and preferred invoice terms?
> 
> -Amelia

From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@skyward.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T08:54:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA baseline exception + latency floors for batch endpoints

Ben, Jasmine —

Thanks, the approach makes sense. A few items for the redline:

- Mixed routes: we’d prefer a traffic-weighted measurement where a route is evaluated as "batch" for a given calendar month if >50% of its tokens were tagged as batch in your telemetry. Can Redwood adopt a monthly determination?
- Credit cap: Skyward is comfortable with 8% for the first 6 months if there's a concrete path to 10% tied to spend threshold; please include the spend thresholds in the redline.
- PO & invoicing: we will share a PO template once SLA language is locked; our preferred terms are Net 45.

We’ll also need a short operational attestation that scheduled batch jobs (nightly scoring) will be considered when investigating incidents to avoid false positives.

If you can get the redline over by tomorrow afternoon we’ll review before Friday legal sync.

Best,
Amelia

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@skyward.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood SLA redline + DocuSign link

Amelia —

Thanks for the clarifications. Attached is Redwood_SLA_Redline_v2.docx which:
- Implements the monthly-determination rule for mixed routes (route is treated as batch for that calendar month if >50% of tokens are tagged batch in our telemetry),
- Calls out the batch exemption when monthly batch token share >30%,
- Adds the 8% cap for months 1–6 and a conditional uplift to 10% if Skyward meets the minimum monthly spend of $75,000,
- Adds a paragraph on operational attestation and our incident review process.

I’ve uploaded the redline to DocuSign for ease of execution: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-redwood-sla. Please note the DocuSign packet includes the SOW placeholder for spend tier and invoice terms. If Net 45 is your required term, please confirm and we’ll update the SOW.

We can also run a 30-minute onboarding call with our SREs during the pilot window to review tagging for batch routes and runbook expectations.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@skyward.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA redline + DocuSign link

Laura —

Received and reviewed. The redline looks good, and the spend threshold is acceptable. We’ll route the DocuSign packet internally today; finance confirmed Net 45 is fine. Please schedule the SRE onboarding for next Tuesday.

Next steps:
- I’ll countersign in DocuSign once legal is back from review (target today)
- Send invoice terms to procurement contact and share PO when ready

Thanks for the quick turnaround — excited to get started.

Best,
Amelia
Head of Procurement, Skyward Analytics
